title: Position a drill on a marked wood block and pull its trigger with the other arm
instruction: Use the right arm to pick up the drill and hold its bit vertically against the red target on the wood. Use the left arm to pull the red trigger while keeping the bit on the target.
context: Parallel grippers can hold a handheld tool but cannot curl a finger around its trigger. This task couples maintaining vertical bit-to-workpiece contact with independent trigger actuation, a prerequisite for handheld-tool use in workshop automation. It evaluates positioning and mechanical actuation; material removal is outside scope.
setup: World coordinates are metres: X forward from the arm bases, Y left, Z up. Two 6-DoF YAM arms with parallel grippers have bases at (0, +0.305, 0.750) and (0, -0.305, 0.750). Both start at joint angles [0, 1, 1, -0.6, 0, 0] radians with 94 mm open jaws. A fixed wood-appearance table is 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m, centred at (0.36, 0, 0.7175); its top is Z=0.7475. A secured solid-wood block, 180 x 140 x 30 mm, is centred at (0.260, -0.080, 0.7625), with top Z=0.7775. A 20 mm diameter red target is centred on its top; its 0.4 mm visual overlay has no collider. The orange/black plastic-housing and metal-chuck drill body is approximately 184.36 x 186.84 x 57.19 mm and 0.5 kg. It starts on its side with the original body bounding-box centre at XY (0.250, -0.300), yaw 90 degrees, chuck pointing along world -Y. A rigid blunt metal probe, 35 mm long and 6 mm diameter, extends the chuck: its model-frame end is (-0.127, -0.0695, 0). The assembled drill/probe extent is about 219.18 x 186.84 x 57.19 mm. A red polymer trigger proxy, 14 x 20 x 40 mm and 15 g, is attached at drill model coordinate (-0.017, -0.017, 0), with 5 mm travel in model +X, 150 N/m return stiffness and 2 N s/m damping. The workpiece securing fixture is approximated by a fixed body. The calibrated station also includes a floor, fixed overhead RGB camera and collision stand/housing, lights, and one RGB camera on each wrist; README documents these shared fixtures and pinned sources. All starts use seed 0, zero jitter, and a 0.5-second settling phase before the trial.
scoring: Evaluate the final state, except that full success must hold for 0.5 seconds (10 consecutive 20 Hz steps). Holding requires the right TCP within 55 mm of the model handle point (0.040, 0.005, 0), jaw gap below 75 mm, and filtered contact force above 0.05 N from EACH right finger against the drill. Upright means bit axis within 12 degrees of vertically down. On target means bit-tip XY error at most 10 mm, absolute height error from the wood top at most 4 mm, and tool-to-wood contact force above 0.05 N. Trigger pressed requires at least 3 mm travel, at most 7 mm including solver tolerance, transverse attachment error below 3 mm, and left-finger-to-trigger contact force above 0.05 N. Forces are averaged over the 12 physics steps in the current control interval. Award 1.0 when holding, upright, on target and trigger pressed hold together for 0.5 seconds. Otherwise: 0 if not holding or no steps; 0.25 if holding but not upright; 0.50 if holding upright but not on target; 0.75 if holding upright on target without full success. The motor and hole are not scored.
run_limit: 1,600 control steps at 20 Hz: 80 seconds of simulation time. Full success ends the run early.
reset_notes: Reset both arms to the open-jaw ready pose, restore the drill and attached trigger, and settle for 0.5 s. Wood and target stay fixed. No material is consumed; starts use seed 0 and zero object jitter.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz with 20 Hz YAM joint commands, frictional grasps, a blunt probe and a spring-return trigger proxy. Workholding is a kinematic wood block; the fixture is not modelled. Contact sensors distinguish the two gripping fingers, wood contact and left-arm trigger contact. Inertias, friction and trigger dimensions are approximations. No motor, cutting, hole formation, chips, heat or deformation is simulated.
